Fourier orthogonality packages the equation p1+p2+p3=N into an integral of a cubic exponential sum, after which the task becomes showing a structured leading contribution dominates a controlled error.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Assuming GRH, the stated asymptotic theorem covers odd N above 10^20. A von Mangoldt-weighted representation function J(N) is associated with prime triples summing to N, an exponentially damped sum S(a) is introduced, and orthogonality rewrites J(N) through an integral involving S(a)^3 plus an error. Positivity of J(N) yields a representation.

directed.conceptual_reading: The proof converts control of a cumulative prime-counting surrogate into existence in a short interval. Its purpose is not only to find a prime, but to force the residual n-p into the finite range needed by the next module.
